title: A TEE-Protected Framework for Explainable LLM-Assisted Microgrid Decision Support
content: Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize heterogeneous operational evidence and communicate recommendations to power-system operators, but hallucination, prompt manipulation, and an untrusted software stack limit their use in critical control settings. This paper proposes a trusted execution environment (TEE)-protected framework for evidence-grounded LLM-assisted microgrid decision support. A tree-based forecaster produces numerical predictions, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identify influential measurements, and an attribution drift monitor summarizes departures from a clean reference. The resulting structured evidence constrains an LLM reasoning layer, while a deterministic policy gate retains final authority over allow, review, or block actions. Model artifacts, prompts, policies, intermediate evidence, and audit records are placed within an attestable execution boundary. A component-level case study on UNSW-MG24 and SDN-MG25 shows similar one-step forecasting accuracy (R2 = 0.9897 and 0.9890) and illustrates the grounding evidence available to the proposed LLM layer. The case study does not instantiate or evaluate an LLM; consequently, no claim is made about LLM reasoning accuracy, security effectiveness, or TEE overhead. The contribution is a bounded architecture and evaluation protocol for future implementation.
